# A return in an event handler ends the handler, wherever it stands: before
# a write, or in a loop. Bubbletea writes a handler into Update's switch, so
# a body that returns is a closure called there, and the return is not
# Update's.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component counter ui.node {
    var title = ""
    var n = 0
    ui.input #name(:value=title)
    ui.button #add(text="Add", @click {
        if title == "" {
            return
        }
        n += 1
    })
    ui.button #upTo(text="Up to 3", @click {
        for var i = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] {
            if i > 3 {
                return
            }
            n += 1
        }
    })
    ui.text #count(value="{n}")
}

func testReturnBeforeAWrite(t test.Test, c counter) {
    c.add.click()
    t.assert(c.count.value == "0")
    c.name.input("x")
    c.add.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.count.value == "1", 2000)
}

func testReturnInALoop(t test.Test, c counter) {
    c.upTo.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.count.value == "3", 2000)
}

ui.window {
    counter
}
-- testrun/bubbletea/go/app.sngl/counter/1 --

      "Desc": "ReturnInALoop",
      "Passed": true
